speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow this down, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The presence of visible hematuria, right flank pain, and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections in a 42-year-old male is highly suggestive of a kidney stone causing obstruction and secondary irritation. While the history of UTIs raises the possibility of an infected stone or struvite formation, the acute presentation of flank pain and blood points primarily to nephrolithiasis. I will proceed with a non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis to confirm the presence, size, and location of any calculi.
